title: Activity Threads & Contextual Roles Sidepanel — compact prototype for RBAC auditing and quick actions
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Prototype a compact sidepanel that surfaces activity threads (grant/revoke events, approvals, and reviewer comments) directly in context with a selected role or user, enabling faster access-review decisions and immediate remediation actions. This explores combining audit-log granularity with quick actions (revoke, request-justification, schedule-expiry) and a lightweight cost-impact snapshot to help admins understand economic implications of temporary elevated access.

Key flows prototyped: (1) Role detail -> sidepanel opens showing the last 10 activity threads with inline timestamps, actor, source (console/API/Dedicated), and evidence links; (2) From a thread, owners can expand a compact timeline, add a justification, or trigger an access review; (3) When toggling a proposed role change we show an estimated quarterly token-cost delta and a qualitative reliability risk hint; (4) Quick revoke and canary rollback actions surface with a single confirm step and optional note that is captured in audit logs.

Design constraints & trade-offs: We prioritized minimal surface area to avoid cluttering the main console list view. Trade-offs considered: (a) showing full permission diffs inline vs. linking to a full diff page — chose inline condensed summary with link to full diff to keep the panel snappy; (b) cost estimator accuracy vs. simplicity — current MVP uses heuristics from usage-history over last 90 days rather than exact forecasting; (c) GDPR/PII considerations — evidence links are obfuscated unless the admin has explicit data access scope.

Accessibility: keyboard-first interactions, ARIA roles for timeline items, color contrast checks for status chips.

Success metrics: time-to-decision during an access review reduced by 30% (baseline from research), reduction in mistaken long-lived grants by 20%, and adoption rate >40% of workspace admins within first 8 weeks.

Next steps: polish edge states (no-activity threads, service-account-only roles), integrate ENG-4502 for backend audit streaming, sync with PM-221 for rollout gating and messaging. Plan to ship as part of console-2026.04 canary for 10% of workspaces behind a feature flag.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Initial draft wireframes uploaded to Figma (see attachments). Wanted to test whether inline cost hints distract from security decisions; early feedback from PM suggests label it as 'Estimated cost impact' to reduce perceived precision.

2026-03-04 — Eng sync: streaming backend can provide real-time threads but needs field-level permission checks (ENG-4502). Decision: MVP will show last 10 events and lazy-load older ones to avoid heavy queries.

2026-03-06 — Research check-in: 5 admins in moderated tests preferred the sidepanel for rapid triage vs opening the full audit page. Requested clearer affordance for 'request justification' that pre-populates reviewer and role context.

2026-03-08 — Design review with Security: must mask user-identifying evidence by default for cross-tenant auditors. Security asked for a review checklist before canary — added security_review_required flag.
2026-03-10 — PD review: minor copy changes to action confirmations; added an optional free-form note captured in audit entries. Ready for design handoff to Eng with annotated Figma specs.
